learning.title: Attribute contract drift before rebinding — a stale base reports main's change as yours
learning.body:
On #498 (2026-11-17) the gate failed with "breaking contract drift at schemas.MergeEntryCreate.properties.checkRunIds.minItems: constraint added", and the PM routed the sanctioned rebind procedure mechanically. dev-web's diagnosis was better: their branch touched zero contract files (git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- packages/contracts schemas was empty) and sat 20 commits behind main — minItems:1 on checkRunIds already existed in origin/main's contracts.json. The gate had compared their STALE BASE against new main and reported main's own change as drift.
Rule: when the drift gate fails, attribute the drift FIRST — (1) diff your branch's own contract/schema files against main (the empty diff means the drift is not yours); (2) grep main's generated contracts for the named constraint — if it exists on main, the fix is `git merge origin/main` + regenerate, never a rebind; (3) rebind only when the constraint is genuinely yours to own — a rebind for someone else's change bakes their approval into your ledger entry and falsifies fromBaseRefs.
Corollary: long-lived branches behind main hit false drift routinely; merge main before running the drift gate so the gate compares your delta, not your age.
